subject: Pricing + Batching: token volumes & continuous batching assumptions
messages:

Subject: Pricing + Batching: post-call recap & next steps

Hi John / Lisa —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on pricing and batching assumptions: 

1) Traffic & volume: you mentioned roughly ~250M tokens/month today across the fraud-detection prompts, with occasional spikes during morning/evening batches. Please confirm if that 250M is request tokens only or includes responses.

2) Latency & pattern: you described a continuous, low-latency stream of small prompts (~60–120 tokens total per request) rather than large batched jobs. That suggests continuous batching will be the dominant optimization.

3) Budget targets / unit economics: you flagged a target of roughly $50–100 / 1M tokens as the range the procurement team is comfortable with. Can you confirm a concrete target number (e.g., $60 / 1M) and the annual commit range that would be required to hit that?

4) Concurrency expectations: you estimated steady-state concurrency around 150–200 qps during peak, with short spikes up to ~500 qps. If you have per-minute histograms or a sample log (a 24–72 hour window) that would help our capacity planning.

5) Next steps I propose:
   - You share a sanitized 48–72 hour traffic sample (timestamps, request tokens, response tokens, QPS).
   - We schedule an hour technical deep-dive (include your infra/ops and our SEs) to validate continuous-batching benefits and latency SLOs.
   - I'll send an initial mutual action plan (attached) and a draft SLA for review.

Attached: MAP_AcmePayments.xlsx (mutual action plan), SLA_Draft.pdf (draft SLA).

If John/Lisa can confirm the target $/1M and whether the 250M includes responses, I can run an estimated unit-cost model and outline options (hosted, dedicated, private) and likely quantization/batching profiles.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Couple quick clarifications from our side:
• The 250M tokens is total tokens (request + response) per month. Peak days are typically ~20% higher.
• Average prompt+response is ~120 tokens (request ~30 tokens, response ~90).
• Steady-state qps is closer to 160, peaks to ~480 for short windows during business hours.
• Latency requirement: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms — the product team is pretty strict on latency.
• Budget: procurement gave a target band of $50–80 / 1M tokens. If we can get to ~$60 / 1M with committed volume, that would be ideal.

Thanks John — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick notes on how we think about the numbers and suggestions before the technical call: 

- Continuous batching expectations: for your workload (many small, steady requests ~120 tokens) continuous batching typically yields the best unit economics. We size the batch window and per-GPU concurrency to balance latency SLOs with token efficiency.

- Example config (initial): batch window 15–25ms, per-GPU concurrency ~64 active streams, adaptive batching to pull immediate tokens during spikes. With ~160 steady qps and 480 spikes, you’d be looking at a few GPUs in dedicated or a modest hosted tier.

- Unit economics & estimates: based on similar customers, and assuming continuous batching with KV/prefix caching and 8-bit quantized model on optimized kernels, a realistic landed cost target to aim for is $40–65 / 1M tokens depending on commit/volume and SLA. With a 12-month commit around 3B tokens we can push toward the lower end ($40–45 / 1M). At 250M/month (3B/year) your target ~$60 / 1M is achievable with a reserved plan.

- Latency: our runtime can meet p50/p95 targets with the config above; the technical deep-dive will validate exact P50/P95 for your model variant and request distribution.

Action items before the call:
1) John: drop the 72-hour sample in the Drive (anonymized).
2) Lisa: please share any hard latency SLO must-haves we need to know.
3) Aditya/SEs: I'll loop you in for the deep technical review.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue Mar 3 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed Mar 4 09:00–10:00 PT. Which works for you?

I'll also prepare a preliminary unit-cost model and include assumptions (batch window, concurrency, quantization) in the shared doc.

Thanks —
Camila
